hints: Focus on how Period 3 oxide reactivity with water changes from left to right across the period.
Recall that $\text{MgO}$ is sparingly soluble and reacts very slowly to give a slightly alkaline solution, while $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is insoluble and amphoteric.
Remember that $\text{SiO}_2$ has a giant covalent structure that water cannot break, so check which numbered statement alone can be true.
walkthrough:
**Recall the trend for Period 3 oxides**

Think of the oxides going from basic on the left to acidic on the right. Reactivity with cold water falls sharply after magnesium.

General idea:
$$\text{basic oxides (Na, Mg) react} \to \text{amphoteric (Al) no reaction} \to \text{acidic giant (Si) no reaction}$$

**Test MgO**

$\text{MgO}$ is only sparingly soluble, but it does react slowly with cold water to form magnesium hydroxide.

$$\text{MgO(s) + H}_2\text{O(l)} \to \text{Mg(OH)}_2\text{(aq, very dilute)}$$

**Test Al2O3 and SiO2**

$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is insoluble with very high lattice energy and does not react with water, it needs acid or concentrated alkali. $\text{SiO}_2$ is giant covalent with strong $\text{Si-O}$ bonds that cold water cannot break, so no reaction.

$$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3 + \text{water} \to \text{no reaction}$$
$$\text{SiO}_2 + \text{water} \to \text{no reaction}$$

**Conclude the combination**

Only statement 1 is true. That corresponds to the 1 only option.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean all three react. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{SiO}_2$ show no reaction with cold water even after one day, so this overestimates their reactivity.
options.B: Incorrect. This would include $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$. Students sometimes think amphoteric means reacts with water, but amphoteric means reacts with acids and alkalis, not with neutral water.
options.C: Incorrect. This would include $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{SiO}_2$ but exclude $\text{MgO}$. It is backwards, as $\text{MgO}$ is the only one of the three that does slowly hydrate to $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$.
options.D: Correct. Only 1 is true. $\text{MgO}$ reacts very slowly with cold water to give a faintly alkaline solution of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$, while $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{SiO}_2$ are insoluble and unreactive toward water.
